page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with the running head centred at the top and the page number at the top right. Dictionary entries in Latin with Hebrew headwords and Hebrew forms. At the bottom right, a catchword in Hebrew.

main_text.p: אַחֲרִית f. Posteritas, Posterius, Postremum, Extre-mum, Ultimum, Finis, Consequens: & metonymicè Merces, ut Prov.23.v.18. Chald. בְּאַחֲרִית יוֹמַיָּא In extremo dierum, Dan.2.28. Aff. לְאַחֲרִיתוֹ Posteritati ejus, Dan.11.4.

אָחַר Moratus est, Tardavit, Distulit, quasi dicas, Posterio-ravit. Fut. וְאֶחַר Et moratus sum, Gen.32.4. forma Chal. cui simile in אזל. Pih. Præter. אִחַר Distulit, Gen.34.19. אִחֲרוּ Differunt, Jud.5.28. cum Segol ab initio loco Tzere, propter sequens Chatephsegol. Hiph. Futur. וַיּוּחַר Et sivit ut tardaret, 2.Sam.20.5. cum ו loco א ex Chaldaismo.
אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִים m. Plural. Satrapæ, Esth.3.9. Constructi. לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ Satrapis regis, Esr.8.36. Chald. אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפַּנַיָּא Satrapæ, Dan.3.2.
אֲחַשְׁתָּרָנִים m. p. Cursores regii; Esth.8.10. juxta quosdam. R. Salom. Jarchi exponit Camelos velocissimos: Aben Esra, Mulos, quem plerique sequuntur.
אטר m. Kynosbaton (Sentis-canis, Rubus caninus) vel Rhamnus, spina summè aculeata, Psal.58.10. אֶל־הָאֵטָר Ad Rhamnum vel Cynosbaton, Jud.9.14.
אטט Sensim, Leniter, Lentè, 1.Reg.21.27. לְאַט לִי Leniter mihi, 2.Sam.18.5. לְאַט Sensim, Jesa.8.6. Aff. לְאַטִּי Ad lentitudinem meam, Lentè, pro commoditate mea, Gen.33.14. Usum habet Nominis.
אטים m. p. Præstigiatores, Divini, Jesa.19.3.

אטם Clausit, Occlusit, Obturavit: Partic. אֹטֵם Occludens, Jesa.31.15. Part.Præt. אֲטוּמִים Clausa, id est, Angusta, quasi Clausæ videantur, secundum Chald. paraphraste, vel Clausæ, scil. vitro, 1.Reg.6.v.4. Et sic Ezech.40.16. Hiph. Futur. יַאְטֵם Obturabit, Psal.58.5.

page.notes: Hebrew headwords and forms are copied from the scan with approximate vowel points where the print is faint; the vowel points in the Hebrew forms are not fully certain. Running head and page number are Hebrew and Arabic as printed. The large Hebrew headwords (אחש, אטר, אטם) are set in a bold display type and are given here as the headword forms.
